beats.t: Even breathing echoed in the mirror corridor. Yeoni's short nasal breaths struck the glass walls and returned in overlapping layers.
Opposite them stood a being with Yeoni's real face. Damp bangs, an old hoodie, a person standing on two legs. It slowly smiled.
Prove it, then.
...Prove what?
That you're the real Yeoni.
The moment those words ended, the entire Island of Companions sank a beat beneath their feet with a heavy thud.
Whoa! Hey, this world has an earthquake option too? I never signed up for that!
Hundreds of floating mirrors flipped over together. Blue letters lit up across their backs, one after another.
[ Island of Companions · Main Trial Begins ]
[ Verifying original identity. ]   [ Time limit 10:00 ]
Yeoni blinked their round eyes. The petals above their head took on a chilly hue in the blue light.
What? Why the sudden identity check? I just logged in.
That's right. With the login rights to your life at stake.
Yeoni's hoof paused. The easy grin drained slowly from their face.
...Login rights?
This is the Island of Companions. It tests whether you can hold your place. Lose that place, and your route home becomes uncertain too.
Wait. Does that mean—
That thing could walk into the real world instead of me?
Yeongnyangi did not answer. Only the tip of the white cat's tail stopped, once. His silence was answer enough.
Quick on the uptake. My brain, after all.
The reflected Yeoni spread both hands. Ten fingers, every joint intact. Wet hair, a hoodie, two legs, the original face. Everything Yeoni had lost.
Yeoni, meanwhile, was a flower pig. Short hooves. Round belly. A single small flower on their head. Far too cute, and far too disadvantaged.
Wow. Is this starting stat gap for real?
If it feels unfair, win.
Hey, don't say obnoxious things with my face. It feels weird.
It's your way of talking too, you know.
...Do I really sound that annoying?
Yes. Very.
Okay. Forced self-awareness achieved. That kind of hurts.
A mirror slid down and stopped right before Yeoni's nose. A sentence appeared on the glass.
Eek, too close! Can you not shove yourself in my face? Personal space, hello?
[ Verification Item 1 · Name ]
An easy question. Yeoni answered at once.
Yeoni.
The mirror gave an unsympathetic double beep.
[ Insufficient ]
...Why? I'm telling you my own name. What's insufficient about that?
I know the name too.
The reflected Yeoni calmly repeated it in exactly the same voice.
Yeoni.
The mirror shone blue, much brighter this time.
[ Two candidates confirmed ]   [ Unable to identify original ]
Hey, Yeongnyangi. Isn't this system's security pathetic? If a name is all it takes, I could hack somebody's account too.
The Companion energies share your own element. Appearance alone cannot tell you whether someone is on your side. That is what makes this difficult.
Why are you only telling me something that important now?
Now is when you need to know.
If you ran customer support, I'd give you one star. Your service is terrible.
There isn't anywhere to leave a rating here. What a shame for you.
A second mirror descended silently. Night-colored darkness slowly spread from within the glass.
[ Verification Item 2 · Memories ]
Yeoni's real life appeared in the mirror. The morning the alarm did not ring. The moment their transit card failed three times at the gate.

The night their assignment corrupted just before submission, leaving them staring numbly at a blinking cursor. A message they deleted instead of sending. An unread reply they checked all day. And the face that smiled as though nothing was wrong.
Yeoni closed their mouth. Each scene was nothing much on its own. But when they arrived together, something inside their chest felt pressed hard beneath a hand.
I was always late.
[ Memory matched ]
When I wanted to speak, it was too late. When I wanted to hold on, I'd already missed my chance. I pretended I was fine, then fell apart alone in my room.
[ Memory matched ]
The flower above Yeoni's head trembled faintly, though there was no wind.
See? I know your whole life too. Beginning to end.
Yeoni pressed their back teeth together. It was true. Every scene belonged to their own memories. They could not deny it.
Yet something was strange. Something remained, like a fish bone lodged in their throat.
The reflected Yeoni was reciting those memories. But all the feelings that had hurt inside them were missing. Like a report on somebody else's life. Meticulous footnotes, not one line of emotion.
...You're right. I was late.
The mirror shivered.
Sometimes I kept my mouth shut when I should have spoken. Sometimes I switched my lock screen on a hundred times waiting for a reply. And plenty of times I smiled like nothing was wrong.
Yeoni laid a short hoof against their round chest.
But inside, I wasn't okay at all.
The reflected Yeoni's face tightened, ever so slightly. As though the flawless report had acquired its first typo.
I wasn't joking because I felt fine. It was because if I didn't laugh, I thought I'd start crying right there.
The mirror blazed.
[ Emotion matched ]   [ Original identity response detected ]
The flower above Yeoni's head brightened. A layer of warmth mingled with the chilly blue light.
...Not bad.
I do know a little about my own story.
Then get the next one right. This one will hurt a little.
A third mirror descended. Unlike the others, it pretended to reflect nothing before an image slowly formed.
[ Verification Item 3 · Present Body ]
A flower pig stood inside the mirror. Pink body. Little flower on its head. Round belly. Short legs. Yeoni themself.
Ah... Still can't get used to that.
Then give up. Make it easy on yourself.
No thanks.
You said you hate that body.
I do. Honestly, I do. No fingers, stumpy legs, oinks coming out of my nose whenever I get startled—
My life's visual balance is completely broken. Plot it on a graph and it's a cliff.
An involuntary little oink slipped out at the end. Yeoni squeezed their eyes shut.
Oh, come on. That one doesn't count.
The system keeps count. That isn't up to us.
See? You hate it too. Something like this can't be your true body.
I hate it.
Yeoni admitted it readily. Then slowly raised their head. Their eyes did not waver in the blue light.
But hating it doesn't mean it isn't me.
The reflected Yeoni's smile stopped abruptly. Yeoni looked straight into the eyes of the flower pig in the mirror.
I don't like how I look. But the one standing here in this corridor instead of running away is me.
The flower above their head lit itself. This time, the light did not come from a mirror.
I'm the one holding on even when I'm scared. The one arguing to the bitter end in this ridiculous situation. The one getting pissed off by what you say. All me.
The mirror shook violently. Hairline cracks raced over its surface.
[ Present self acknowledged ]   [ Original identity response increasing ]
A green shoot popped through the glass floor directly beneath Yeoni's hoof. Smaller than a fingernail. But unmistakable.
Take it. Now.
Their body moved before thought. Yeoni reached out a short hoof. The moment the shoot touched it, warmth seeped into their body.
What... is this?
Eul Wood. The first character of your Day Pillar, its Heavenly Stem.
The green shoot swayed gently on Yeoni's hoof, as though breathing.
Small grasses, flowers, vines. They may not look powerful, but they do not die easily. They bend instead of breaking, then grow again.
Yeoni looked down at their hoof. Still no fingers. Yet strangely, a sense of holding something tightly remained. One tiny root. Thin, but alive.
The reflected Yeoni's face hardened, cold as ice.
At the outstretched hand, the scattered mirror fragments gathered again like iron filings. This time they formed not curves, but honed, razor-sharp blades.
Be careful. Rob Wealth is moving now.
Rob Wealth? What's that supposed to be?
Energy like your own. Yet a force that takes what belongs to you. It wears a sibling's face and tries to claim a share of what is yours.
That's right. Even that little shoot you barely managed to get—I can take it.
Dozens of blades rose around the reflected Yeoni in a fan. Then all of them rained toward Yeoni.

Yeongnyangi sprang up. Golden claws slashed the air. Clang! Clang! Clang! The blades scattered, then instantly gathered again. Shatter them and they returned. Cut them and they flew again. There was no end.
Yeongnyangi!
I can open a path! But I cannot protect your characters in your place!
At that shout, the reflected Yeoni reached toward them. The energy of [乙] nestled in Yeoni's hoof began to shake, like a tiny shoot about to be pulled out, soil and all.
Hey, this... It's slipping out!
Rob Wealth! If you cannot call what is yours your own, it will be taken!
What's so special about one little blade of grass?
At those words, the light of [乙] visibly weakened. Yeoni looked down at the trembling shoot.
A tiny thing that seemed ready to snap underfoot or blow away in a single gust. And yet its leaves still trembled with life.
It may be small, but it's mine.
The fading light of [乙] revived. The reflected Yeoni's eyebrow twitched.
Even if it looks weak, it's mine. It doesn't need your stamp of approval to belong to me.
The flower on Yeoni's head bloomed brightly. Green vines shot out beneath their hooves.
The vines threaded among mirror fragments and coiled around each incoming blade. Clatter! The blades stopped dead in midair.
...Good.
Huh? What did I just do?
You used Eul.
Oh, did I get a skill? Have I awakened?
Something like that.
Can I name it? I was thinking 'Little Sprout, Please Hang In There.'
Not now. And not that name, ever.
Why so firm? Show some respect for my naming sense.
Then how about 'Weed'? Short, punchy, easy to remember.
No.
An oink escaped Yeoni's nostrils in protest. Nobody took their side.
The reflected Yeoni clenched their teeth. For the first time, unease crossed the formerly relaxed face.
...It isn't over yet.
The other Yeoni lowered a hand, and the final mirror drifted forward. It was different from the rest.
Black water filled it. This time, even Yeoni could not bluff.
The water lay perfectly quiet, without a single ripple. That stillness only made it more chilling.
Eul alone does not complete Eulhae.
...Is that Hae?
Yes. Hae is deep water. Midwinter water. On the surface, still as though frozen, but holding a great deal within.
The black water in the mirror slowly stirred. From its depths came a muffled voice.
[ ...Come down. ]

Yeoni stiffened. This was unlike the black hands that had chased them across the river. Not an enemy attacking from outside, but something quietly calling from within. Deep, cold feelings they kept wanting to avoid.
You can't go in there.
...Why?
You hate going deep.
Yeoni had no immediate comeback. No wisecrack, no meme, nothing.
When your thoughts get heavy, you deliberately change the subject. You act funny because you're afraid you'll fall apart alone. And you only admit what really hurts long after it happens.
That water has been inside you from the beginning.

Scenes rose in the black water. A night waiting for a reply. A long message finished but never sent. A chat closed and muted while pretending not to care. A face staring at the ceiling, alone in bed in a dark room.
Yeoni's breath caught. It hurt more than anything the reflection had said. Because all of it was real. Not one detail embellished.
You found Eul. But if you turn away from Hae, your Eulhae Day Pillar will remain incomplete.
...What happens then?
You reclaim only half of your center. You return to reality incomplete.
Yeoni stared at the last mirror. Black water. Deep water. Somewhere at its bottom, the second character waited quietly.
Yeoni tightened their hooves. Still no fingers. But now they thought they understood a little. Fingers were not the only way to hold on to something.
You can't go.
Why do you keep telling me what I can't do?
Because you're afraid.
Does being afraid mean I can't do it?
You... always let it.
I told you not to say things like that with my face.
Why? Because it's true?
No. It being true makes it even more annoying.
The reflected Yeoni thrust out a hand. Black water spilled over the final mirror's frame. A roaring rush covered the corridor floor in an instant.
Yeoni tried to dodge, too late. Cold water wrapped around their short hooves and climbed above their ankles.
Yeongnyangi!
Yeongnyangi leaped. His claws blazed gold and cleaved the black water vertically. It parted, then rejoined as though nothing had happened.
Cutting won't work on this!
Then what am I supposed to do!
Do not run!
If I don't run now, I'm going under!
Run, and it grows deeper!
The reflected Yeoni stood on top of the black water, shoes dry, not even a toe wet.
Exactly. Run, and it gets deeper. Just like you've always done.

The black water dragged Yeoni's round body downward. They dug their clawless hooves against the floor. But their body was small and their strength insufficient. They were afraid. Real fear, the kind no joke could cover.
[ Come down. Stop pretending you're fine. Look at the feelings you buried. ]
Yeoni squeezed their eyes shut. At that moment, warmth spread inside a hoof. The [乙] they had just reclaimed. The warmth of a tiny shoot.
Yeoni opened their eyes. A green vine grew beneath their hoof again. But it did not push back the black water. Instead, it rooted itself in the water.
Yes! That's it!
Are you sure? I'm putting roots into the water right now!
Eul does not grow by avoiding water. It takes water in and grows!
Why are you only giving me the instruction manual now!
Because you only just showed me!
The vine was thin. A flick of a fingertip looked enough to snap it. Yet even when black water crashed over it, it bent once, then stubbornly lifted its head again.
Yeoni caught their breath at the sight. Small. Apparently weak. Yet alive. Just like Yeoni right now.
Stop.
No.
Yeoni planted their hooves more firmly. From below, the vine's roots held the body the current kept pushing away.
I'm still scared. But you taking my name because I'm scared—I hate that more.
The black water surged. Inside the last mirror, a single character appeared faintly, like water mist.

Still far away. Too deep to reach with an outstretched hoof. But clearly visible. The flower above Yeoni's head trembled. The shoot of [乙] was carefully sinking its roots toward the black water of [亥].
Stop it!
The reflected Yeoni shouted for the first time. There was no ease left in that voice.
A huge wave rose inside the final mirror. Black water towered like a wall and yanked Yeoni forward.
Grab me!
Yeongnyangi rushed over and caught Yeoni's hoof in his mouth. It did not hurt. But the water was too strong. The white cat's small body was dragged along too.
Then go down there yourself.
The last mirror swung wide like a door. Black water poured like a waterfall. Yeoni gritted their teeth and held on. At last, their entire body was sucked forward.
OINK—AAAAH!
This time it was not an act. Not a comic snort, but a scream of genuine fright.
Don't let go of your name! Hold on to Eul!
Yeoni gripped the warmth inside their hoof with everything they had. There were no fingers. Still, they held tight in their heart.
Just before being pulled under, Yeoni caught one last glimpse of the human standing outside the mirror. The reflection was smiling. But there was no confidence left in that smile.
Let's see whether you can still say you're yourself, even in the deep water.
Yeoni fell endlessly through the black water. The flower on their head shone brightly one final time.
And in the deepest darkness, the second character, asleep until now, quietly opened its eyes.
[ The Abyss of Hae Water was opening. ]
